RjD1aLm4Thg.summary: Michael Levin's NeurIPS 2018 talk on bioelectric computation outside the nervous system, showing how cell electrical networks shape development and regeneration. It covers morphological information processing in living tissue.
RjD1aLm4Thg.why: HN regularly calls it mind-blowing and recommends it as an introduction to Levin's work on bioelectricity and regeneration.

RIctzAQOe44.summary: Daniel Stone, a longtime X and Wayland developer, explains at linux.conf.au 2013 why X11's design became untenable and what motivated Wayland. The talk walks through X's history and accumulated cruft.
RIctzAQOe44.why: HN treats it as the definitive, funny and educational answer to why X could not be fixed, and links it in almost every Wayland vs X argument.

ROor6_NGIWU.summary: Rich Hickey's 2013 talk applies language-design thinking to whole systems, covering names, queues, data, failure, and the interfaces between programs. It ends with a call to action for building systems holistically.
ROor6_NGIWU.why: HN recommends it as a key Hickey talk on system design that changes how people think about distributed state and interfaces.

R7EEoWg6Ekk.summary: Christopher Domas's Derbycon 2015 talk on the M/o/Vfuscator, a compiler that emits only x86 mov instructions, showing mov is Turing complete. It explains how a full machine is built from mov and why the output is a nightmare to reverse engineer.
R7EEoWg6Ekk.why: HN calls it a legendary, clearly explained hacker talk whenever mov-only computing or anti-decompilation comes up.

R9ITLdmfdLI.summary: Paul Graham's keynote at PyCon 2012, in which he talks about startup ideas and what kinds of companies are likely to matter in the future. He discusses ideas such as a better email client and a search engine for hackers, and argues for looking back at the present from the future.
R9ITLdmfdLI.why: HN commenters return to it as a worldview-shaping talk whose predictions about technology and startup ideas turned out to be prescient.

RNFesa01llk.summary: Thunderf00t, a physicist, critically assesses the Hyperloop concept, covering the vacuum, pressure, safety, and cost problems of high-speed tube travel. He argues the media accepted the claims uncritically.
RNFesa01llk.why: HN repeatedly cites it as the best skeptical engineering analysis of why Hyperloop is impractical.

RuOvn4UqznU.summary: Cardiologist Dr. Pradip Jamnadas lectures on the rationale for dietary restriction and fasting, covering insulin resistance, glucose intolerance, and low-carb eating over about 81 minutes.
RuOvn4UqznU.why: Several HN commenters call it one of the best explanations of fasting and insulin and recommend it in diet and weight loss threads.

RSTNhvDGbYI.summary: Technology Connections explains how old-fashioned non-electronic rice cookers work, using a magnet and spring switch tripped by the Curie point. It shows the thermodynamics and magnetism behind a simple appliance.
RSTNhvDGbYI.why: HN recommends it as a delightful breakdown of the cleverness in dumb appliances and an entry point to the channel.

RqQhWitJ1As.summary: Andrew "bunnie" Huang examines how realistic hardware supply chain attacks are, from rogue insiders to nation states, in the wake of the Bloomberg Businessweek report. He explains how undocumented components could be hidden on boards and how hard they are to spot.
RqQhWitJ1As.why: HN people point to it as the sober, technically grounded picture of hardware supply chain security, and an eye-opening one.

R2Aa4PivG0g.summary: Peter Alvaro's Strange Loop 2015 talk argues that query languages let you state what you mean, and applies that to distributed programming. It covers Datalog, Dedalus and the Bloom lineage for reasoning about distributed systems.
R2Aa4PivG0g.why: Recommended as a fantastic introduction to declarative and Datalog-based distributed systems and failure modeling.

RaI_TuISSJE.summary: Allieway Audio gives an informal introduction and live-coding demo of ORCA, a free esoteric programming environment for building procedural sequencers from Hundred Rabbits. It walks through the interface and how to make music with it.
RaI_TuISSJE.why: HN commenters call it the best video overview of Orca, the explanation that makes the unusual interface click.

RWTic9btP38.summary: Together Louisiana asks why Louisiana stays poor despite its natural resources and industry, focusing on industrial tax exemptions and corporate welfare.
RWTic9btP38.why: Linked in threads on corporate tax incentives and subsidies as a detailed example of how they can trap a state.

RfdZTZQvuCo.summary: A short clip of Penn and Teller arguing, in blunt and profane language, for vaccination and against anti-vaccine claims. It covers risk versus benefit and herd immunity.
RfdZTZQvuCo.why: HN commenters share it in vaccine threads as a quick, entertaining explanation of vaccination in layman's terms.

RrHnLXMTOWM.summary: Bill Hammack of engineerguy introduces his series on Michael Faraday's lectures on The Chemical History of a Candle. He describes the free companion book and the commentary and caption features that help modern viewers.
RrHnLXMTOWM.why: Praised as a masterpiece of science education that recreates Faraday's demonstrations.

RKT-sKtR970.summary: AngeTheGreat describes building a physically realistic internal combustion engine simulator in C++, drawing on fluid dynamics, physics and chemistry. It generates procedural audio for engines such as a V8.
RKT-sKtR970.why: HN points to it as a standout example of physics-based sound synthesis and engine simulation.

RMxB7zA-e4Y.summary: Technology Connections explains that the so-called EV charger in an electric car's charging cable or wall unit is really an EVSE, a smart switch that safely delivers AC power. The actual charger is inside the car. The video covers the safety signaling and mechanisms involved.
RMxB7zA-e4Y.why: HN recommends it as the clearest introduction to what is inside an AC EV charging station and why it is much simpler than people assume.

RQY6WGOoYis.summary: Not Just Bikes explains the Downs-Thomson paradox using Amsterdam and Toronto: road widening doesn't fix congestion, and buses stuck in traffic make transit slow. It argues for giving transit its own priority infrastructure.
RQY6WGOoYis.why: HN points to it as a clear introduction to why widening roads fails and why transit-only lanes matter.

RmIgJ64z6Y4.summary: Charles Stross's 34C3 talk on how science fiction gets the future wrong. He argues that corporations are slow, human-powered AIs that optimize for profit, and that regulation lags behind accelerating technology.
RmIgJ64z6Y4.why: HN returns to it whenever corporations as paperclip-maximizer AIs or AI risk come up.

RrpajcAgR1E.summary: Dick Hardt's fast-paced OSCON keynote on Identity 2.0 and the move toward user-centric digital identity. It is also famous for its rapid-fire, many-slide presentation style.
RrpajcAgR1E.why: HN commenters hold it up as one of the most engaging tech talks ever given, both for its identity ideas and its slide technique.

RuCnZClWwpQ.summary: A 105-minute film of a West African smith family in Burkina Faso smelting iron from ore, from making charcoal and building the kiln to forging tools. It is a cultural recreation filmed for the camera, not current practice.
RuCnZClWwpQ.why: Recommended as an amazing documentary of traditional ironmaking, often used as a baseline for the labor required.

R3xX37RGJKE.summary: Yaron Minsky of Jane Street shows how the OCaml Incremental library lets trading UIs express data transformations that are easy to read and efficient on streaming data. It includes a live table demo.
R3xX37RGJKE.why: Recommended in incremental computation and reactive UI threads as the best conceptual overview of Incremental and incr_dom.

REni8Oi1QJQ.summary: Not Just Bikes takes on the common excuse that a country is simply too big or spread out for good transit and walkable cities. The video argues that city density and short everyday trips matter, not national size or overall population density.
REni8Oi1QJQ.why: HN users cite it as the standard rebuttal whenever someone says that America is too big for rail or good urban design.

RQv5CVELG3U.summary: Sabine Hossenfelder explains the delayed choice quantum eraser and argues it does not rewrite the past, as popular accounts claim. She walks through what the experiment actually shows.
RQv5CVELG3U.why: HN recommends it as a clear debunking of the retrocausality interpretation of the quantum eraser.

RTB5XhjbgZA.summary: Posy explores segmented displays, from the seven-segment display to alternative designs with fewer or more segments, with patents and history.
RTB5XhjbgZA.why: Recommended as a meditative, geeky tour of alternative display designs.

RUwS1uAdUcI.summary: In this TED talk, Hans Rosling uses animated statistics to debunk myths about the developing world, showing how health and income have improved across countries.
RUwS1uAdUcI.why: Cited as the classic data-driven argument that the first-world versus third-world split is outdated and the world is improving.

Ra_0DgnJ1uQ.summary: Not Just Bikes explains why cars rarely crash into buildings in the Netherlands, attributing it to street design that forgives mistakes and to systematic crash investigation. It contrasts this with North American acceptance of such crashes.
Ra_0DgnJ1uQ.why: HN cites it for the systems-over-blame view of road safety and for Dutch infrastructure design.

RlXdsyctD50.summary: A PBS Space Time episode introducing de Broglie-Bohm pilot wave theory, an interpretation of quantum mechanics that avoids much of the strangeness of the mainstream views. It is aimed at curious lay viewers.
RlXdsyctD50.why: HN commenters regularly send people to it as an accessible, friendly introduction whenever pilot wave theory comes up.

RxD6H3ri8RI.summary: Ian Hubert shows quick, unconventional tricks for greenscreen compositing in Blender, as a follow-up to his motion tracking video.
RxD6H3ri8RI.why: Recommended as a favorite among practical Blender guides from a hugely productive solo artist.

RCRTgtpC-Go.summary: A very long video essay by Shaun on the decisions and motivations behind the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki, with a detailed timeline and argument that they were not militarily necessary.
RCRTgtpC-Go.why: HN recommends it as a thorough, nuanced account of why the bombings happened and what led Japan to surrender.

ReRcHdeUG9Y.summary: Simon Sinek's 99U talk on why leaders earn trust by putting their team's safety ahead of their own, drawing on biology and anthropology. It distills the ideas of his book Leaders Eat Last into about 46 minutes.
ReRcHdeUG9Y.why: HN commenters point to it as a quick way to get the key concepts of the book and as an introduction to leadership thinking.

RjfbvDXpFls.summary: Mario Zechner explains why he built pi, a minimal coding agent, out of frustration with existing agent harnesses. He also discusses how AI agents are straining open source projects and argues for slowing down.
RjfbvDXpFls.why: HN commenters recommend it as a first-hand argument for building your own lean agent harness instead of relying on bloated, vendor-controlled ones.

RCCigccBzIU.summary: A 2001 VPRO Noorderlicht documentary episode, filmed in Austin in 2000, visiting Edsger Dijkstra and his views on thinking as a discipline. It is in Dutch with English subtitles.
RCCigccBzIU.why: Recommended as a short documentary that shows the human side of Dijkstra.

RhdlBHHimeM.summary: Glenn Vanderburg asks whether software development can be real engineering, surveying other engineering disciplines and decades of programming experience. He envisions what a software engineering worthy of the name might look like.
RhdlBHHimeM.why: HN recommends it in debates about software engineering rigor, agile, and formal methods.

RtWbpyjJqrU.summary: Destin of Smarter Every Day films a cat falling in high-speed slow motion to show how cats right themselves in midair, and introduces the physics behind it.
RtWbpyjJqrU.why: HN recommends it as a good visual explanation of how cats land on their feet.

RxabLA7UQ9k.summary: Hans Zimmer's 'Time', the closing piece from the Inception soundtrack, set to a static image.
RxabLA7UQ9k.why: Recommended as powerful soundtrack music, including for listening while coding.

RzWB5jL5RX0.summary: Dr Mike Pound of Computerphile shows how a modern laptop can crack Enigma, using a ciphertext-only attack based on an older paper. He compares it with the tooling in CrypTool.
RzWB5jL5RX0.why: HN recommends it as a good starting point on practical Enigma cryptanalysis with modern hardware.

R37zkizucPU.summary: Louis CK speaks at a 2010 NYPL tribute to George Carlin about how Carlin's habit of discarding material and writing a new hour each year changed his own career. He becomes emotional describing it.
R37zkizucPU.why: HN finds the story inspiring beyond comedy: getting good by throwing out your old work and starting over.

R3ZJKN_5M44.summary: A 2006 Saturday Night Live fake infomercial with Steve Martin and Amy Poehler selling the sure-fire way out of debt: don't buy stuff.
R3ZJKN_5M44.why: HN posts it as a favorite comic summary of debt avoidance and spending discipline, and as a joke in buy-now-pay-later threads.

RNsEsZbXE-4.summary: RustConf 2020 closing keynote by Sian Griffin that dives into Pokemon Blue glitches, notably Missingno and arbitrary-code-execution tricks. It uses them to explain how memory unsafety works and how memory-safe languages like Rust prevent such bugs.
RNsEsZbXE-4.why: HN points to it as a fun, technically deep talk that makes memory-safety bugs vivid through a beloved game.

Rqfkuc5mawg.summary: The first episode of Nathan Barley, Chris Morris and Charlie Brooker's British sitcom satirizing hip media and startup scenesters in mid-2000s Shoreditch. Cynical writer Dan Ashcroft finds himself idolized by the moronic Nathan Barley.
Rqfkuc5mawg.why: Recommended as a savage, ahead-of-its-time parody of startup and tech culture.

R13BD8qKeTg.summary: Veritasium explains Bayes' theorem with examples and introduces the 'Bayesian trap', where repeated events get mistaken for inevitable ones. It discusses how priors shape our expectations and behavior.
R13BD8qKeTg.why: HN points to it as an accessible introduction to Bayesian reasoning and as inspiration for personal projects.

R2_Mn-qRKjA.summary: A short clip from the Season 2 finale of BoJack Horseman in which a character says that doing the hard thing every day gets easier. It is set to a Courtney Barnett song.
R2_Mn-qRKjA.why: HN shares it as encouragement in threads about habits, discipline, and social anxiety.

R2paSGQRwvo.summary: Lindybeige gives an hour-long history of English coinage and the problems of maintaining a trustworthy currency. It ends with an explanation of why the pounds, shillings and pence system worked so well.
R2paSGQRwvo.why: Pointed to as the best explanation of pre-decimal British money, including forgery and the guinea.

R3bo-s_OY4Q.summary: Yanis Varoufakis argues that Europe's electricity price spikes stem from how the energy market was designed and privatised, plus corporate profiteering. He proposes ways out.
R3bo-s_OY4Q.why: Cited in UK and European electricity price threads as an explanation of marginal pricing and market design.

R9c-_neaxeU.summary: Matt Parker of Stand-up Maths demonstrates MENACE, Donald Michie's 1961 machine made of matchboxes that learns to play noughts and crosses through reinforcement. He builds and trains a physical version.
R9c-_neaxeU.why: HN cites it as a fun, tangible way to teach machine learning, including to kids.

RLySXTIBS3c.summary: The climactic orange juice futures trading scene from the film Trading Places, in which the heroes corner the market on the trading floor.
RLySXTIBS3c.why: Cited as an accessible depiction of how commodity trading and the trading pit work.

RcGyVTAoXEU.summary: Psychologist Kelly McGonigal argues in this TED talk that stress is harmful mainly if you believe it is, and that reaching out to others is an underrated way to reduce its effects.
RcGyVTAoXEU.why: HN mentions it when discussing how believing stress is harmful affects health and anxiety.

RijGNytjbOI.summary: Scott Arciszewski's DEF CON 26 Crypto and Privacy Village talk critiquing the JOSE standards (JWT, JWS, JWE) and showing how to design cryptographic tokens more safely.
RijGNytjbOI.why: HN recommends it as the video version of the argument that JOSE/JWT is a flawed standard, and as a help in understanding token design choices.

RoGuvvzHY1A.summary: Kirsten Dirksen tours the underground ferro-cement dome home of Paula and Bill Lishman, the family behind the geese-led flight story. The skylit earth-sheltered house stays warm below the frost line.
RoGuvvzHY1A.why: HN points to it as an interesting real-world example of earth-sheltered living for staying cool or warm.

RGw6fXprV9U.summary: NileRed makes radioactive uranium glass from scratch, showing the chemistry involved and the green fluorescence under a blacklight. The video includes warnings about handling radioactive material.
RGw6fXprV9U.why: HN recommends it as an informative and entertaining look at how uranium glass is actually made.

RVU62CQTXFI.summary: A 1979 CBC radio interview in which Ted Nelson tries to explain how computers could serve as tools for thinking and visualizing. The interviewer keeps failing to grasp the idea, and Nelson patiently answers again and again.
RVU62CQTXFI.why: HN cites it as a vivid record of how alien personal computing and hypertext sounded to a skeptical public, and as a favorite Nelson interview.

RXJKdh1KZ0w.summary: A spoof industrial promo for the Rockwell Retro Encabulator, a deadpan stream of technobabble about an imaginary machine. It is a classic engineering in-joke.
RXJKdh1KZ0w.why: HN uses it as a joke whenever jargon-heavy or meaningless technical pitches appear, and praises it as a masterclass in technobabble.

Rybpaqhg5Qg.summary: Fully Charged's first of three reports from the Orkney Islands, covering the Surf 'n' Turf project that uses surplus wind and tidal power for hydrogen and electric vehicles.
Rybpaqhg5Qg.why: HN cites it for Orkney's surplus renewable energy, hydrogen facilities and EV uptake.

R0JKCYZ8hng.summary: A short TED-Ed animated lesson by Anita Collins on what happens in the brain when people play a musical instrument. It argues that playing engages many brain areas at once, like a full-body workout, with long-term benefits.
R0JKCYZ8hng.why: Cited as a source for claims that learning an instrument connects both brain hemispheres, though some commenters note they haven't verified it.

R35UuntQQF8.summary: A 256-byte MS-DOS intro that renders a raymarched, procedural 3D animation. It won the 256-byte competition at Riverwash 2009 and the scene.org award for best technical achievement that year, and the author published commented x86 assembly source.
R35UuntQQF8.why: HN commenters cite it as the most impressive 256-byte production and as an example of how much graphics code can fit in a tiny binary.

R35gWBtLCYg.summary: Simone Giertz presents Truckla, a homemade pickup truck conversion of a Tesla Model 3, shown in a short humorous promo.
R35gWBtLCYg.why: HN mentions it as a favorite homemade EV pickup, often as an honorable mention in electric truck discussions.

R5Gppi-O3a8.summary: A three-minute excerpt from Milton Friedman's Free to Choose in which he uses a pencil to show that no single person knows how to make it. He argues that the free market coordinates countless strangers peacefully.
R5Gppi-O3a8.why: HN uses it as the canonical illustration of decentralized production and global cooperation, often cited well outside economics threads.

RBBiri3CD6w.summary: A short unscripted demo of writing FizzBuzz in JavaScript with a generator function on a steno keyboard, typos included. It gives a feel for what real coding in stenography looks like.
RBBiri3CD6w.why: Whenever HN asks whether you can program with steno, this is the go-to demo showing it working.

RIvL2ONhFBI.summary: Rob Pike presents the Go 2 draft specifications at the Sydney Golang Meetup, covering the Go 2 process and several proposals including generics. The Q&A contains a well-known exchange about the name of the language.
RIvL2ONhFBI.why: Cited in Go threads for Pike's stance on generics and the Go 2 process, plus an amusing Q&A moment.

RJVL80Gg3lA.summary: A Google Tech Talk by Laurens van der Maaten, co-creator of t-SNE, on visualizing high-dimensional data by mapping it to two dimensions. It explains how the technique works and how it compares with other visualization approaches.
RJVL80Gg3lA.why: HN people point to it as the canonical explanation from the method's author whenever t-SNE comes up.

RJh9yTIBY48.summary: The Explosions&Fire channel taste-tests the chloride salts of the alkali metals (lithium through cesium), plus some alkaline earth metals and ammonium. The presenter describes the flavors, and the results are more pleasant than expected.
RJh9yTIBY48.why: It gets linked in threads about salt and taste as a quirky, memorable curiosity.

RKXZ7t_RiOE.summary: The Futur's guide to pricing design and creative work, arguing against hourly rates and for value-based pricing. It features Blair Enns and says to price the client, not the job.
RKXZ7t_RiOE.why: Recommended in threads on freelance design pricing and why large corporations pay a lot for branding work.

RMWNvwLiXIQ.summary: Tantacrul tells the story of Audacity, the widely used free audio editor, and announces his involvement in the project. It includes an interview with the original developers and a look at the software's usability.
RMWNvwLiXIQ.why: HN recommends it during the Muse Group acquisition controversy for its funny, pragmatic take on usability and open source stewardship.

RPdB_zdyMbM.summary: Starstruck, an AGA Amiga demo by The Black Lotus that won first place at Assembly 2006, shown in HD at 50fps.
RPdB_zdyMbM.why: Shared as an example of great Amiga demoscene work.

RQSBj2LKkWg.summary: 2kliksphilip examines UserBenchmark, a hardware comparison site known for strongly biased, pro-Intel writing. The video explains the site's credibility problems and points viewers to better sources for CPU and GPU information.
RQSBj2LKkWg.why: HN uses it as the go-to link to warn people not to trust UserBenchmark for hardware comparisons.

RcU7FaEEzNU.summary: The Brass Eye special 'Paedogeddon!' by Chris Morris, a black-comedy satire of British media moral panic that duped celebrities and politicians into endorsing nonsense. It is the final episode of the series.
RcU7FaEEzNU.why: HN cites it as the classic satire of moral panics, especially when child-safety or illegal-image legislation is discussed.

RcVA8Nj6HEo.summary: 2swap explores lambda calculus using John Tromp's lambda diagrams, with animated beta-reductions, asking what PLUS times PLUS gives. It touches on Church encodings and the equivalence of Turing machines and lambda calculus.
RcVA8Nj6HEo.why: Mentioned in lambda calculus and combinator threads as a visual entry point to the topic.

RhsUHDJ0BFM.summary: A short clip from Breaking Bad in which Saul Goodman teaches Jesse Pinkman how a cash-heavy business like a nail salon can launder drug money.
RhsUHDJ0BFM.why: HN uses it as a quick, memorable illustration of how money laundering works in discussions of crypto seizures and mixers.

RkTvDjhImwo.summary: A three-minute demo of a series circuit with three LEDs that behaves in a surprising way, posed as a question of how it works.
RkTvDjhImwo.why: Cited as an example of how much surprising behavior can hide in seemingly simple circuits, in hardware backdoor discussions.

RwRZtZQoLtQ.summary: Chamath Palihapitiya talks with Jason Calacanis about how he bought into the mythology of Silicon Valley, which he calls a Ponzi scheme, and about rebuilding Social Capital. He urges founders to grow slowly and build what matters.
RwRZtZQoLtQ.why: HN cites it for Chamath's claim that venture-backed growth resembles a Ponzi scheme, especially when startups spend heavily on big-tech advertising.

RyMdOT8YJgY.summary: Tom Scott's Ignite London talk about a flash mob that went very wrong.
RyMdOT8YJgY.why: Recommended as an excellent short Ignite talk from a geek comedian.

R2idkNdKqpQ.summary: Douglas Crockford's code::dive 2022 talk on what the next programming language should look like. He presents ideas behind his Misty language, including message-passing actors.
R2idkNdKqpQ.why: HN cites it as Crockford's main explanation of Misty and his take on the actor model.

R706isyDrqI.summary: Apple's famous 1984 Macintosh television commercial, which casts the company as a rebel breaking a Big Brother-style conformity.
R706isyDrqI.why: Cited ironically or as a joke when Apple is accused of becoming the controlling Big Brother it once mocked.

RAGcDi0DRtU.summary: Finnish comedian Ismo does a stand-up routine on Conan about the many meanings of the English word 'ass'. He riffs on the confusing quirks of English as a second language.
RAGcDi0DRtU.why: Mostly posted as a joke or amusing aside in threads about English, language learning, and swearing.

REWeBzGuzCc.summary: A CNN clip from February 2002 of Donald Rumsfeld explaining the idea of known knowns, known unknowns, and unknown unknowns at a press briefing.
REWeBzGuzCc.why: HN links it as the original footage of the famous framing of knowledge and ignorance.

RFO6ZhUW38w.summary: A short live performance of Tim Minchin's comedic song about skepticism, from his DVD 'So Live'. It argues that open-mindedness shouldn't go so far that your brain falls out.
RFO6ZhUW38w.why: HN commenters cite it as a quick, witty reference whenever someone warns against being so open-minded that you become gullible.

RM0uvgHKZe8.summary: A short clip of Madeleine Albright saying the price of the deaths of Iraqi children from sanctions was worth it, uploaded with political commentary about Iran.
RM0uvgHKZe8.why: HN commenters cite the clip critically as evidence of US sanctions policy and its human cost.

ROlDmux7Tk4.summary: A 2008 comedic rap musical pitting Wall Street bankers against consultants, produced by Leveraged Sell-Out.
ROlDmux7Tk4.why: HN mostly uses it as a joke or period reference for banker stereotypes.

RRh0QiXyZSk.summary: The classic 1950s recording of Tennessee Ernie Ford singing 'Sixteen Tons', a song about a coal miner trapped in company-store debt.
RRh0QiXyZSk.why: Used as a joke reference in threads about debt, housing, and exploitative economic arrangements.

RS27u6IqWt0.summary: Short archival film footage of an 87-year-old farmer interviewed in 1929, born in 1842, talking about life and change.
RS27u6IqWt0.why: Used as an anecdote of an old person's views on technological change, such as the telegraph as a distraction.

RWsx1X8PV_A.summary: A short clip of Milton Friedman on the Donahue show answering whether greed is a vice specific to capitalism, arguing it exists in every system.
RWsx1X8PV_A.why: Used as a quick reference clip in capitalism and greed debates.

RXeOiIDNNek.summary: Apple's WWDC 2024 keynote introducing Apple Intelligence along with iOS 18, iPadOS 18, macOS Sequoia, watchOS 11 and visionOS 2.
RXeOiIDNNek.why: HN links to specific segments of the keynote to back up claims about features like Passwords, Math Notes and the ChatGPT handoff.

RY93kr8PaC4.summary: A short IEEE Spectrum clip of Stanford's autonomous car Junior learning to powerslide into a parking spot. It shows several approaches to the maneuver.
RY93kr8PaC4.why: Cited as a simple example of automated driving maneuvers beyond what human drivers can do.

RZtZia4ZkX8.summary: A restored 1994 video of Karl Sims' research on evolved virtual creatures, where simulated block creatures are bred through artificial evolution to swim, walk, follow and compete. It is a landmark demonstration of genetic algorithms in physics simulation.
RZtZia4ZkX8.why: HN brings it up as a classic example of evolutionary algorithms, including how the creatures exploited physics-simulation bugs, which parallels metric gaming in AI.

R_hlMK7tCks.summary: The stoning scene from Monty Python's Life of Brian, where a man is condemned for blasphemy after saying 'Jehovah' over a halibut supper.
R_hlMK7tCks.why: HN uses it as a joke reference in discussions about speech and political correctness.

Ra_khhzuFlE.summary: Footage of Boeing test pilot Tex Johnson barrel-rolling the Boeing 707 prototype over Lake Washington, followed by his explanation of the stunt.
Ra_khhzuFlE.why: HN cites it as a famous bit of aviation history showing the roll was a gentle 1G maneuver and salesmanship.

RjrEQaG5jPM.summary: A short 2006 clip of chaotic traffic in India, with cars, bikes and pedestrians weaving around each other and one car going against the flow.
RjrEQaG5jPM.why: HN uses it as the classic example of chaotic Indian traffic, especially in threads about self-driving cars and spontaneous order on roads.

RkP_OGDCLY0.summary: A clip from Mr. Show season 3 in which characters insist that 24 is the highest number. It is a short absurdist sketch about counting.
RkP_OGDCLY0.why: Posted as a joke in threads about naming large numbers and the size of infinity.

RnIvhlKT7SY.summary: A short promotional video of a 5-axis CNC machine milling an elaborate helmet, made by DAISHIN SEIKI with a DMG machine and hyperMILL CAM software. It shows what 5-axis machining can produce.
RnIvhlKT7SY.why: HN uses it as a go-to example of impressive 5-axis machining and CAM-controlled toolpaths.

RnofCyaWhI0.summary: A compilation of hover tests of exoatmospheric kill vehicles, the small rocket-propelled interceptors used in missile defense, including early prototypes from the late 1980s. It shows the vehicles maneuvering with thrusters in test facilities.
RnofCyaWhI0.why: HN cites it as footage of what thruster-driven interceptors look like, including as a mundane comparison for odd-looking motion in UFO videos.

RoHxyweJcZI.summary: A two-minute 2011 clip of an early uBeam wireless power demo. It shows a short-range ultrasound charging demonstration.
RoHxyweJcZI.why: Cited mainly as a baseline showing uBeam had made little visible progress and as an example of a demo skeptics found unconvincing.

RqvuEal2P2E.summary: Music YouTuber Rick Beato describes confronting the people behind copyright blocks on one of his videos. The video is a rant about how takedowns and demonetization hit music education channels.
RqvuEal2P2E.why: HN cites it as an example of creators' complaints about YouTube copyright blocks on music instruction videos.

Rr8ljRgcJNM.summary: The official music video for Rammstein's 2004 song Amerika, a satirical take on American cultural dominance and its export around the world. It was shot in the ruins of a former chemical site near Berlin.
Rr8ljRgcJNM.why: HN mostly cites it as a pop-culture reference in discussions of American cultural influence, sometimes jokingly.

RuVS7MsQk4Y.summary: Breaking Taps tries to build semiconductor fabrication capability at home, working through decades of lithography history while chasing one-micrometer features. It documents the equipment, process steps and many setbacks along the way.
RuVS7MsQk4Y.why: HN points to it as an example of hobbyist, at-home integrated circuit fabrication.

RvZ-667CEdo.summary: A look at AT&T's 1993 You Will ad campaign, which showed technologies such as video calls and telemedicine that were then under development. It explains the story behind ads that anticipated much of today's technology.
RvZ-667CEdo.why: Cited as a prescient example of predicting the future, though AT&T did not deliver it.

Rw8gE3lnpLQ.summary: An Onion News Network satire about a Warcraft sequel in which you play a character who is playing Warcraft, in a cramped dark apartment.
Rw8gE3lnpLQ.why: Only used as a joke reference when threads feature recursive or nested games and simulations.

RwkNnMrsx7Q.summary: CNN clip of Howard Dean's loud yell at a 2004 Iowa campaign event, which gained wide notoriety.
RwkNnMrsx7Q.why: Mostly cited as an example of how a single unflattering clip can sink a campaign.

RybNI0KB1bg.summary: A short Simpsons clip of Helen Lovejoy shrieking 'Think of the children!', the show's parody of moral panic.
RybNI0KB1bg.why: Used as a joke reply in threads about child-safety justifications for surveillance and censorship laws.
